what_it_does: High-speed optical cables (>100 gigabits per second) carry data using multitone modulation—like how different musical instruments play different frequencies simultaneously. This receiver converts those analog tones into digital signals. The traditional approach tries to equalize (correct) the signal using a fixed digital filter with dozens of taps before sending it to the decoder, which is complex and power-hungry. This paper uses a different strategy: it converts the signal with a time-based analog-to-digital converter, then applies per-tone equalization digitally, avoiding the need for massive analog filter complexity.
